entries.title: Fine particles outdoors
entries.description: WHO estimated 4.2 million premature deaths worldwide from outdoor air pollution in 2019; this is a modeled population burden.
entries.keywords: air Fine particles outdoors Fine airborne particles are inhaled from varied sources such as fires, transport, industry and combustion.

entries.title: Polluting household cooking fuels
entries.description: WHO reported about 2.1 billion people worldwide cook using polluting fuels or technologies in its December 2025 fact sheet.
entries.keywords: air Polluting household cooking fuels Burning wood, coal, kerosene or other polluting fuels indoors can create harmful airborne particles.

entries.title: Lead in drinking water
entries.description: WHO states that no level of lead exposure is known to be without harmful effects; young children are especially vulnerable.
entries.keywords: water Lead in drinking water Lead can leach from service lines, solder and plumbing; exposure also occurs through dust, paint and industrial sources.

entries.title: PFAS in water and food
entries.description: NIH reviews associations between exposure to certain PFAS and immune, cholesterol, reproductive and other effects; evidence differs among chemicals.
entries.keywords: water PFAS in water and food Some PFAS can reach people through drinking water, food and occupational or product-related routes.

entries.title: Arsenic in groundwater
entries.description: WHO identifies long-term inorganic arsenic exposure through drinking water as a cause of cancer and other harmful outcomes.
entries.keywords: water Arsenic in groundwater Natural geology can introduce arsenic into aquifers used for drinking, cooking and irrigation.

entries.title: Methylmercury in fish
entries.description: WHO identifies methylmercury as a concern for fetal and early-childhood neurological development; some fish accumulate more than others.
entries.keywords: food-waste Methylmercury in fish Mercury can transform in aquatic ecosystems, build up in fish and reach people through seafood.

entries.title: Electronic waste and unsafe recycling
entries.description: WHO reports 62 million tonnes of e-waste generated globally in 2022; just 22.3% was documented as formally collected and recycled.
entries.keywords: food-waste Electronic waste and unsafe recycling Unsafe burning, dismantling and dumping can expose workers and communities to hazardous air, dust, soil and water mixtures.

entries.title: Radon inside buildings
entries.description: U.S. EPA identifies radon as a naturally occurring radioactive gas that can cause lung cancer; it cannot be seen or smelled.
entries.keywords: home-work Radon inside buildings Radon can enter buildings from soil and accumulate indoors; actual concentration differs by building.

entries.title: Heat and preventable illness
entries.description: CDC describes heat exhaustion, heat stroke and other heat-related illness risks, with greater danger in certain health and working conditions.
entries.keywords: home-work Heat and preventable illness Indoor or outdoor heat, physical activity and barriers to cooling can overwhelm the body's temperature control.

entries.title: Respirable silica at work
entries.description: CDC/NIOSH warns that breathing respirable crystalline silica during certain jobs can lead to silicosis and other serious diseases.
entries.keywords: home-work Respirable silica at work Cutting, drilling, grinding and polishing some stone and other materials can produce fine respirable silica dust.

entries.title: WHO ambient air quality database
entries.description: Annual average PM2.5, PM10 and nitrogen dioxide concentrations for selected settlements. A historical city-wide annual mean is not today's local AQI or a personal exposure measurement.
entries.keywords: World Health Organization City and town measurements from 127 WHO members, associate members or territories; not every settlement. June 2026 version, observations from 2010–2024

entries.title: AirNow air-quality information
entries.description: AQI levels, smoke information and health-oriented air-quality categories. A monitor or sensor does not identify all local exposures, individual doses or a responsible facility.
entries.keywords: U.S. EPA and partner agencies U.S. location-level monitors and forecasts; availability varies by place and pollutant. Current/forecast AQI with real-time data caveats

entries.title: EPA ECHO facility compliance
entries.description: Facility permit details, inspection records, reported violations and enforcement actions. A listed violation can be alleged rather than finally adjudicated; missing records do not prove a facility is safe.
entries.keywords: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Facilities recorded in applicable EPA and state/tribal environmental reporting systems. Mixed enforcement, permit and reporting windows

entries.title: EPA Toxics Release Inventory
entries.description: Reported chemical releases, waste transfers and pollution-prevention information. Pounds released are not a measured population dose or toxicity ranking, and some tools may be offline.
entries.keywords: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Facilities and chemicals meeting TRI reporting rules, not every source of pollution. Annual self-reported releases; the EPA toolbox lists current tool status

entries.title: Annual drinking-water quality reports
entries.description: Water sources, reported regulated contaminants, violations and supplier contacts. A supplier-wide report cannot substitute for a qualified lead or other contaminant test at one tap.
entries.keywords: U.S. EPA and local public water systems Community public-water suppliers; not a private well or a household's individual tap. Annual reports from water suppliers

entries.title: European Air Quality Index
entries.description: Short-term air quality estimates for PM2.5, PM10, NO2, ozone and SO2. The Index is not a legal compliance determination or a long-term annual air-quality assessment.
entries.keywords: European Environment Agency European monitoring stations and modeled air-quality areas; data availability varies. Near-real-time station information and model forecasts

entries.title: European Industrial Emissions Portal
entries.description: Reported industrial releases to air, water and land, transfers of waste and facility details. An annual reported mass does not show local exposure or prove legal responsibility.
entries.keywords: European Environment Agency Major industrial complexes under covered European reporting requirements, not all businesses. Annual facility and pollutant reports; check reporting year

entries.title: Canadian Air Quality Health Index
entries.description: A health-oriented indicator based on air pollutant measurements and forecast conditions. A community AQHI is not an individual exposure estimate and local conditions can vary.
entries.keywords: Environment and Climate Change Canada Canadian AQHI reporting communities; station and location coverage varies. Current conditions and forecasts

entries.title: National Pollutant Release Inventory
entries.description: Facility-reported air, water, and land releases, disposals and transfers. Preliminary data can contain reporting errors; facility releases are not individual dose measurements.
entries.keywords: Government of Canada Reporting facilities and substances under NPRI thresholds across Canada. 2025 records are labeled preliminary in the current search tool

entries.title: Check air quality in the UK
entries.description: Air quality by locality or postcode, alerts and exposure guidance. A local forecast is an indicator, not a personal diagnosis or source-attribution model.
entries.keywords: UK Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs Area-level air forecasts and available monitors in the UK. Current monitoring and forecasts where provided

entries.title: Environment Agency Pollution Inventory
entries.description: Reported annual releases to air and water and waste movements from qualifying sites. Large sites are covered selectively; reported annual masses do not describe personal exposure.
entries.keywords: Environment Agency / UK National Data Library Regulated major industrial sites in England within the inventory's reporting scope. Downloadable annual data for 2013–2024 at the time of review

entries.title: Australian National Pollutant Inventory
entries.description: Annual releases and waste transfers of listed NPI pollutants, including facility mapping. Different chemicals cannot be summed into a meaningful total-harm ranking; reported release is not confirmed exposure.
entries.keywords: Australian Government DCCEEW Australian facilities and diffuse sources within NPI reporting rules. 2024–25 reporting period, updates/corrections possible

entries.title: An emitted kilogram is not a human dose
entries.description: A facility-reported mass tells you a quantity released, not what any person inhaled, swallowed or absorbed.
entries.keywords: An emitted kilogram is not a human dose measurement Reported quantities require fate, transport, concentration, exposure-route and toxicity evidence before inferring health risk. Which chemical, release medium and exposure point could connect this inventory to an actual dose? Reading the data

entries.title: Corporate production attribution is not a facility map
entries.description: Carbon Majors attributes production-linked greenhouse gases to fossil-fuel and cement producers, including the combustion of sold products outside their home jurisdictions.
entries.keywords: Corporate production attribution is not a facility map measurement That methodology does not locate every emission at the producer's headquarters or establish a locally measured toxic release. Does the figure include downstream combustion, and where did the physical activity occur? Reading the data

entries.title: National inventories and producer totals are different ledgers
entries.description: A territory-based country inventory assigns emissions to places; Carbon Majors assigns production-linked activity to producer entities.
entries.keywords: National inventories and producer totals are different ledgers measurement Adding, ranking or dividing these figures as if they share the same denominator creates misleading comparisons. Do the two datasets use the same year, gases, spatial boundary and scope? Reading the data

entries.title: A number without its unit and year is not a finding
entries.description: Environmental sources can report annual tonnes released, concentrations, global CO₂-equivalents or historical totals. Each answers a different question.
entries.keywords: A number without its unit and year is not a finding measurement An annual mass cannot be compared directly with a concentration, and a historical estimate is not a live condition. Can the unit, time interval, geographic boundary and version be written beside every figure? Reading the data

entries.title: Measured and modeled exposure are different evidence
entries.description: Exposure assessments may rely on direct monitoring, indirect estimation or reconstruction, depending on data and study design.
entries.keywords: Measured and modeled exposure are different evidence measurement A modeled estimate is not a personal measurement; a single sensor may not represent other times or locations. What was measured directly, what was inferred, and what uncertainties accompany both? Reading the data

entries.title: A screening flag is a reason to investigate
entries.description: Screening and refined exposure assessments serve different purposes. A preliminary indicator can help decide what requires a closer look.
entries.keywords: A screening flag is a reason to investigate measurement A screening-level result is not, by itself, a demonstrated injury, causal link or legal conclusion. What evidence and quality controls would a refined assessment need? Reading the data

entries.title: The five links of an exposure pathway
entries.description: ATSDR evaluates contaminant source, environmental fate and transport, exposure point, exposure route, and potentially exposed population.
entries.keywords: The five links of an exposure pathway pathways Knowing an industrial source exists does not establish that contamination reached anyone. Which of the five links is directly documented, and which remains unknown? How pollutants move

entries.title: Potential and completed pathways are not synonyms
entries.description: ATSDR distinguishes potential pathways, where one or more elements remain uncertain, from completed pathways, where all five elements are present.
entries.keywords: Potential and completed pathways are not synonyms pathways Potential is not proof of contact; completed contact is not proof that injury followed. What evidence establishes the pathway at the relevant place and time? How pollutants move

entries.title: Even completed exposure does not establish harm
entries.description: A completed ATSDR pathway describes an exposure opportunity or contact; further scientific evaluation considers dose, toxicity, duration and health effects.
entries.keywords: Even completed exposure does not establish harm pathways A pathway classification cannot be converted directly into numbers of illnesses or assigned blame. What independent exposure and effect evidence would be needed next? How pollutants move

entries.title: Groundwater can move dissolved contamination
entries.description: USGS explains that natural and human-generated substances can enter groundwater as water moves through soil and rock; transport depends on site conditions.
entries.keywords: Groundwater can move dissolved contamination pathways A nearby industrial operation alone does not establish that contamination reached a particular well. What do local flow direction, well depth, sampling dates and analytes show? How pollutants move

entries.title: Clear-looking groundwater is not proof of safe chemistry
entries.description: Groundwater can appear clear while containing dissolved natural or human-generated constituents.
entries.keywords: Clear-looking groundwater is not proof of safe chemistry pathways Appearance cannot substitute for properly collected samples and laboratory analysis of relevant contaminants. Is this a private well or public system, and which substances were actually tested? How pollutants move

entries.title: Mercury can concentrate up aquatic food webs
entries.description: NOAA describes conversion of mercury to methylmercury and its accumulation and magnification through feeding relationships.
entries.keywords: Mercury can concentrate up aquatic food webs pathways A fish species name alone does not establish a particular meal's concentration or a specific source of pollution. What species, location, advisory and contaminant-testing evidence apply? How pollutants move

entries.title: Hazard is not the same as risk
entries.description: Hazard identification asks whether a substance can cause an adverse effect. Risk characterization also needs relevant dose-response and exposure evidence.
entries.keywords: Hazard is not the same as risk health The fact that a chemical can be toxic does not quantify an individual's risk at an unspecified dose. Which exposure conditions make the hazard relevant to this population? Health & risk

entries.title: Four parts of a defensible health-risk assessment
entries.description: EPA describes hazard identification, dose-response assessment, exposure assessment and risk characterization as distinct components.
entries.keywords: Four parts of a defensible health-risk assessment health Skipping steps can turn a plausible concern into an unsupported numerical claim. Which component has measured evidence and which still rests on assumptions? Health & risk

entries.title: Dose depends on more than one reading
entries.description: Exposure assessment considers magnitude, frequency, duration, route and the exposed population, along with data quality and uncertainty.
entries.keywords: Dose depends on more than one reading health A single point reading cannot establish a lifetime exposure or diagnose a particular health outcome. What time series, duration, location and exposure-route evidence are available? Health & risk

entries.title: The vulnerable life stage can change the analysis
entries.description: EPA's lead risk research considers how exposure and adverse outcomes can differ across critical life stages and how risk management may reduce harm.
entries.keywords: The vulnerable life stage can change the analysis health A community-average value cannot describe a particular child's exposure or medical condition. Which population, medium, sampling method and life stage does the evidence actually cover? Health & risk

entries.title: PFAS is a family, not a single test result
entries.description: NIH reviews different health associations for PFAS exposures; individual compounds, exposure routes and scientific evidence can differ.
entries.keywords: PFAS is a family, not a single test result health A label that says only 'PFAS' is insufficient for a compound-specific risk or source attribution. Which named PFAS, units, method, detection limits and reporting date were used? Health & risk

entries.title: Radon risk depends on the building and measurement
entries.description: EPA provides guidance on testing indoor radon and reducing elevated levels; a building-specific result is needed to understand its conditions.
entries.keywords: Radon risk depends on the building and measurement health County maps or a neighbor's result cannot establish one room's radon concentration. Was a suitable indoor test performed, and how long did it sample? Health & risk

entries.title: A daily air index is not an annual exposure profile
entries.description: AirNow provides current and forecast air-quality information; WHO's city database describes historical annual concentrations where available.
entries.keywords: A daily air index is not an annual exposure profile health Today's AQI and a historical city annual mean answer different questions and cannot describe individual dose alone. What monitoring site, averaging period, pollutant and date are being compared? Health & risk

entries.title: A supplier report does not measure every household tap
entries.description: EPA's Consumer Confidence Reports describe public water system information and reported quality; local plumbing and private wells can require distinct assessment.
entries.keywords: A supplier report does not measure every household tap records A system-wide report is not a certified measurement from a particular kitchen faucet or private well. Who supplies the water and where would a valid point-of-use sample be collected? Public records & accountability

entries.title: A reporting inventory leaves things out
entries.description: EPA notes that TRI reporting covers specified chemicals and facilities under reporting requirements, not every source of exposure.
entries.keywords: A reporting inventory leaves things out records No entry in the inventory does not prove that an area is pollution-free or that a facility has no emissions. Was this facility or activity within reporting scope for the substance and year? Public records & accountability

entries.title: An enforcement record needs its procedural status
entries.description: EPA ECHO provides inspections, permits, compliance and enforcement records that researchers can use to investigate facilities.
entries.keywords: An enforcement record needs its procedural status records An alleged or recorded violation must not automatically be described as a final adjudication or a personal health outcome. What agency action, date, facility identifier and final disposition are documented? Public records & accountability

entries.title: Money paid, promised and capped are not interchangeable
entries.description: Publicly reported remedies can include completed payments, future schedules, settlement obligations and maximum caps. POISONERS separates these in its evidence ledger.
entries.keywords: Money paid, promised and capped are not interchangeable records Adding overlapping amounts, changing currencies without method or treating a promise as money already paid misstates the record. Which legal instrument, date, original currency and paid-status disclosure supports the amount? Public records & accountability

entries.title: A public record is not a liability finding
entries.description: An emissions inventory, monitoring result and enforcement entry are different classes of evidence and do not by themselves answer every legal causation question.
entries.keywords: A public record is not a liability finding records Do not infer wrongdoing, fault or individual culpability solely from appearance in a dataset or job title. Which jurisdiction, legally established elements and adjudicated findings are actually documented? Public records & accountability
